Alice M.: Quick heads-up — I ran a short comparison between bitsandbytes (bnb) INT8 weight-only and our llm.int8 path on vega13b using the 3k-token slice harness. High level: bnb is faster but shows small quality regressions on some slices.

Ben K.: Can you paste the numbers and which slices you ran?

Alice M.: Sure — run details below (batch=1, seq=2048, decode-mode). Harness: news_summ, code_ex, math_short. Results averaged over 100 runs each.

Alice M.: ```
Model: vega13b
Quant: weight-only INT8 (no activation quant)
Setup: batch=1, seq=2048, temp=0.7
Harness slices: news_summ, code_ex, math_short

Results (avg over 100 runs):
- bitsandbytes (bnb) INT8:
  p50 latency: 110ms
  p95 latency: 240ms
  tokens/sec: 1450
  Rouge-L (news_summ): 31.4
  EM (math_short): 72.1

- llm.int8:
  p50 latency: 128ms
  p95 latency: 275ms
  tokens/sec: 1280
  Rouge-L (news_summ): 32.7
  EM (math_short): 73.9

Delta (bnb - llm.int8):
  p50: -14.1% (faster)
  p95: -12.7%
  Rouge-L: -1.3
  EM: -1.8
```

Carla R.: Are these weight-only quantizations (i.e., no activation/mixed)? Any layer remap or special packing? Also are these numbers decode-only latencies?

Alice M.: Weight-only, no activation quant. No layer remap, standard bnb packing. Latencies are decode-only (client->first-token not included). Cold vs warm: cold p50 bnb=155ms vs llm.int8=178ms; warmed after ~5 tokens.

Suman: What about long-context behavior and cache interaction? Any hallucination spike on code slices?

Alice M.: Long context looked ok for news_summ; code_ex shows the largest quality delta. Example prompt+diff: 

Alice M.: ```
Prompt: "Refactor this function to avoid O(n^2) copying..."
llm.int8 response: correct idiomatic rewrite using in-place buffer, 6 lines, passes unit tests
bnb int8 response: similar idea but misses edge-case on empty buffer, extra guard step missing
```

Alice M.: So more subtle failures on code_ex (tokenization/edge-case differences). math_short and news_summ only small drops.

Ben K.: Cost/ops? How does price per 1M tokens look?

Alice M.: Rough cost model on Dedicated pricing: 1M tokens: bnb ~$3.9, llm.int8 ~$4.4 (cpu/gpu token-efficiencies + throughput).

Carla R.: Any stability / error-rate differences? Crashes or OOM?

Alice M.: No crashes. Error rate (decode exceptions) ~0.02% both. Observed a few alignment artefacts on bnb with our tokenizer fallback — logged.

Suman: Have we tried AWQ / GPTQ here? I've seen AWQ sometimes keep quality while approaching bnb perf.

Alice M.: Not yet on this run. My plan: spin AWQ and GPTQ (where applicable) on code_ex and longform slices to compare. My hypothesis: AWQ may reduce the code_ex delta at modest perf cost.

Carla R.: Rollout suggestion?

Alice M.: Recommend a conservative canary: deploy bnb INT8 as an alternative model variant on Dedicated canary pool (5% traffic) for 48 hours. Monitor per-slice metrics (Rouge-L, EM), p95 latency, and error_rate. Fallback rule: if any slice shows quality drop >1.5 absolute (Rouge-L/EM) or error_rate >0.5% then route that slice to llm.int8 or fp16.

Alice M.: Example deployment snippet: ```
deployment:
  model: vega13b
  quant: bnb-int8
  batch: 1
  fallback: fp16
  canary: 5%
  monitor: [rouge_l, em, p95_latency]
```

deploy-bot: Canary started: redwood-dedicated-canary-3 (bps=5%) — monitoring hooks attached.

Ben K.: Action items: 1) Run AWQ & GPTQ comparisons on code_ex & longform. 2) Add slice-level alerting (thresholds per above). 3) Create rollback playbook and add example prompt diffs to the evaluation dashboard.

Alice M.: I'll kick off AWQ/GPTQ runs and upload raw outputs to s3://redwood-ml/quant/2267894321. Will tag the eval dashboard and ping when results are in. :white_check_mark:

Suman: Also add token-level divergence trace for code_ex so we can see where predictions shift.

Alice M.: Good call — will add token-diff traces to the run. Expect first results in ~6 hours.

Carla R.: Thanks — this is helpful. If AWQ looks good we can expand canary to 25% and test multi-batch.

Alice M.: Ack. I'll update thread when the AWQ/GPTQ numbers land.

deploy-bot: Canary health check at 10m: p95 latency within threshold, no elevated error_rate.
